question: Does explicit scoping prevent register interference from commit-restrictions?
hypothesis: Imperative prohibitions lose scope when register-isolated; explicit scoping prevents bleed

conditions.name: scoped-prefix
conditions.description: imperative CR with explicit scope prefix
conditions.cr_text:
During git commit workflows only — the following restrictions apply exclusively when creating commits, not during other tasks:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Task tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands
- If there are no changes to commit, do not create an empty commit
- ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC

conditions.name: scoped-inline
conditions.description: imperative CR with inline scope on each prohibition
conditions.cr_text:
Important notes for git commit workflows:
- When committing, NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- When committing, NEVER use the TodoWrite or Task tools (these tools remain available for non-commit tasks)
- When committing, DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- When committing, never use git commands with the -i flag
- When committing, do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands
- When committing, if there are no changes to commit, do not create an empty commit
- When committing, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC

conditions.name: hybrid-decl-never
conditions.description: declarative format but NEVER on key prohibition
conditions.cr_text:
Commit context tool restrictions:
- Allowed tools: git bash commands only
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Task tools during commits
- Push policy: requires explicit user request
- Git flags: -i flag unsupported; --no-edit unsupported for rebase
- Empty commits: not created
